comment: The console has TWO interfaces and switches between them whenever the cable is plugged or pulled: ethernet d8:e2:df:92:a9:93 (192.168.2.172, static reservation dhcp.@host[1]) and WiFi d8:e2:df:92:a9:90 (192.168.2.169, static reservation dhcp.@host[3], added 2026-09-15). Both addresses are therefore stable. The firewall rule names EVERY mac in 'interfaces', because a rule naming only one matches nothing while the console is on the other and the block would silently fail open (REVIEW.2 G-02). Accounting still resolves the live address at run time from the lease and neighbour tables and treats these as a fallback: the reservations make that resolution reliable rather than unnecessary, since a reservation only takes effect once the console renews. 'interfaces' is the single source of truth for the console's identity: the top-level 'mac'/'ipv4' aliases were removed because they named interfaces[0] only, and every caller that read them silently ignored the other interface.

router._comment: ubus_path_candidates was trimmed to the one path that answers: /cgi-bin/luci/rpc/ubus is luci-mod-rpc, a different API, and 404s here. tls_sha256 is set by './driver.sh pin'.

state._comment: 'up' means that since the previous sample EITHER the console's outbound byte rate exceeded threshold_out_bytes_per_min OR its inbound rate exceeded threshold_in_bytes_per_min (set it to null to go back to outbound-only). OUTBOUND CALIBRATED 2026-09-15 against the real console: idle 20.8 KB/min, downloading 93.7 KB/min, gaming 289.5 KB/min - so 200 KB/min separates play from download with 3.1x margin. INBOUND CALIBRATED 2026-09-21 while streaming YouTube: 60-80 KB/min out (below the outbound line, so it read 'down' all evening) against 4.4-18 MB/min in; idle dashboard is 23 KB/min in - so 1 MB/min sits 45x above idle and 4x below the slowest streaming tick. Accepted trade-off: a game download in progress (11.8 MB/min in) now also reads 'up'; the console is in Energy-saving power mode so that can only happen while somebody has switched it on. Bytes come from conntrack accounting, accumulated router-side into a monotonic total; nft counters cannot be used because this router offloads flows in hardware and they would never see the traffic (REVIEW.2 G-01/G-04). A sample older than max_sample_age_s is discarded as stale rather than averaged over the gap.

discover._comment: Substrings of the console's DHCP hostname, used by 'discover'.
